task.title: Deliver one-command customer EKS deployment CLI
task.description: Implement #555 as the sole customer EKS provisioner by extending the shipped metrum-smartrouterctl. One deploy invocation must create or resume one isolated licensed Router from an approved profile and reference-only intent, while plan/status/delete and config or release updates share one normalized idempotent lifecycle. Reuse validated staging discovery and delivery contracts behind typed adapters; do not create a second provisioner, registry, activation authority, or smoke framework.
actions: Add strict versioned reference-only deployment manifest/profile schemas and normalized relational deployment jobs, attempts, resources, approvals, and safe status records.
Implement idempotent plan, deploy, status, and separately authorized delete in metrum-smartrouterctl with fake-first AWS, EKS, RDS, release, secret, license, and Router adapters.

Compose existing EKS discovery, immutable-image delivery, isolation, migration compatibility, license/config revision, activation, exact-host routing, retry, retention, and cleanup contracts without staging-specific hardcoding.

Treat configuration or release changes as a new approved immutable intent reconciled by the same deploy lifecycle; never accept or persist raw config, credentials, DSNs, kubeconfigs, license payloads, or shell commands.
acceptance: One metrum-smartrouterctl deploy command creates or resumes one isolated licensed non-production Router without manual aws, kubectl, RDS, DNS, certificate, secret, license, or workload steps after invocation.

Plan is deterministic and read-only; deploy/status/delete are profile- and job-scoped, bounded, redacted, idempotent, and safe under duplicate, concurrent, timeout, partial-failure, retry, and unknown ownership cases.
Config and release updates pin exact approved config/license revisions and one immutable image digest across retries; no serving Host route or ready state exists before activation passes.

Namespace identity, least-privilege RBAC, network isolation, resource limits, dedicated private RDS/PVC, secret references, license, Router, shared wildcard TLS, and exact Host routing are automated and verified.

All #555 standalone suites, disposable non-production EKS E2E, and independent security/operations review pass before live deploy is enabled; production profiles remain rejected until #518 authorizes them.
evidence: cmd/metrum-smartrouterctl/main.go currently exposes register, observe-schema, quota-reserve, and local status; deploy, promote, and rollback exit disabled.

internal/router/tenant_instance_registry.go explicitly has no AWS, Kubernetes, DNS, RDS endpoint, router database, secret, or live quota adapter; scripts/eks_delivery.py is staging-policy-bound and is not the shipped customer CLI.
GitHub #555 is the open canonical implementation epic; #581 is closed for the safe fake-adapter slice, #507 is complete, and #545, #586, and #518 remain open cross-cutting dependencies.
task.status_reason: Pending: #555 is open, but the shipped CLI implements only the completed #581 local safe-contract slice; deploy/promote/rollback are disabled, scripts/eks_delivery.py is a source-only target-locked staging runner, and no #555 manifest, durable job, live adapter, standalone test-target, or disposable customer EKS E2E implementation exists.
next_steps: Implement the #555 strict manifest/profile/job schema and fake-adapter contract, security, and activation suites in the shipped CLI without enabling live mutation.
Adapt validated EKS discovery and delivery primitives behind typed instance-scoped adapters, then prove retries, config updates, retention, and exact-host activation locally.
Run the approved disposable non-production EKS E2E and independent security/operations review before enabling deploy; keep production profiles blocked on #518.

At execution time, resolve latest build to the clean reviewed origin/main commit, build the matching node architecture, validate package and supply-chain evidence, publish only to the approved ECR repository, and pin the resulting repository@sha256 digest plus safe build timestamp and version evidence.

Inside the protected deployment boundary, read the authoritative production Compose config and env sources without printing them; reproduce the same provider catalog, model-group definitions, routing weights, request-shape metadata, and upstream provider API-key values in a separate demo runtime Secret.

Rewrite every deployment-specific value for demo1: generate distinct caller and browser-admin credentials, bind a non-production instance-specific license, use a fresh private database and state PVC, set the exact hostname and trusted proxies, and keep production tokens, hashes, DSN, license/state, usage records, and customer data out of demo1.

Run the future metrum-smartrouterctl plan against the approved demo profile and strict reference-only intent; review deterministic resources, immutable digest/config/license revisions, ownership, retention, rollback, and sanitized evidence before separately authorized deploy.

Invoke exactly one idempotent metrum-smartrouterctl deploy with the reviewed profile, intent, and intent ID; create or resume the isolated namespace, RBAC, NetworkPolicy, resource limits, PVC, dedicated private RDS binding, runtime Secret references, Router workload, and Service without ambient kubeconfig or manual follow-up mutations.

Require health, readiness, license/config binding, migration compatibility, database TLS, isolation, and protected activation to pass before creating the exact demo1.apps.metrum.ai Ingress Host rule; verify wildcard TLS, wrong-host/default-backend denial, and no production or staging route change.

Compare the safe model-group name set from the demo caller's /v1/models with the protected production caller's allowed set, then run bounded direct upstream and demo Router smokes for every exposed group according to declared capabilities across OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, streaming usage, tools, and image inputs where applicable.

Run real Codex CLI and Claude Code CLI acceptance against a deployment-defined coding group, verify ordinary caller /metrics returns 403 metrics-forbidden, and confirm relational usage/attempt/error/cost evidence without prompts, outputs, images, tools, credentials, token hashes, or full config.

Record sanitized outcome and rollback evidence. On failure remove/disable only the exact demo Host route, observe before retry, and retain RDS/PVC by default; cleanup requires a separate exact-job approval and must not affect production, staging, shared ingress, wildcard TLS, or upstream credentials.

task.title: Deliver one-command customer EKS deployment CLI
task.description: Implement #555 as the sole customer EKS provisioner by extending the shipped metrum-smartrouterctl. One deploy invocation must create or resume one isolated licensed Router from an approved profile and reference-only intent, while plan/status/delete and config or release updates share one normalized idempotent lifecycle. Reuse validated staging discovery and delivery contracts behind typed adapters; do not create a second provisioner, registry, activation authority, or smoke framework.
actions: Add strict versioned reference-only deployment manifest/profile schemas and normalized relational deployment jobs, attempts, resources, approvals, and safe status records.
Implement idempotent plan, deploy, status, and separately authorized delete in metrum-smartrouterctl with fake-first AWS, EKS, RDS, release, secret, license, and Router adapters.

Compose existing EKS discovery, immutable-image delivery, isolation, migration compatibility, license/config revision, activation, exact-host routing, retry, retention, and cleanup contracts without staging-specific hardcoding.

Treat configuration or release changes as a new approved immutable intent reconciled by the same deploy lifecycle; never accept or persist raw config, credentials, DSNs, kubeconfigs, license payloads, or shell commands.
acceptance: One metrum-smartrouterctl deploy command creates or resumes one isolated licensed non-production Router without manual aws, kubectl, RDS, DNS, certificate, secret, license, or workload steps after invocation.

Plan is deterministic and read-only; deploy/status/delete are profile- and job-scoped, bounded, redacted, idempotent, and safe under duplicate, concurrent, timeout, partial-failure, retry, and unknown ownership cases.
Config and release updates pin exact approved config/license revisions and one immutable image digest across retries; no serving Host route or ready state exists before activation passes.

Namespace identity, least-privilege RBAC, network isolation, resource limits, dedicated private RDS/PVC, secret references, license, Router, shared wildcard TLS, and exact Host routing are automated and verified.

All #555 standalone suites, disposable non-production EKS E2E, and independent security/operations review pass before live deploy is enabled; production profiles remain rejected until #518 authorizes them.
evidence: 2026-08-07: protected preflight and immutable-digest staging apply passed after safe clean cutover; usage migration ledger reports state=current, data_version=1, historical-usage-validation-v1=validated; Deployment rollout succeeded with router plus Linkerd init/sidecar; public /readyz returned 200 and unauthenticated /v1/models returned 401. The current source profile was denied protected caller-token read, so no caller credential was exposed.
task.status_reason: Implementation work is active under the existing external validation gate: #555 is being converted from the local fake/RDS lifecycle to real typed AWS EKS and Kubernetes adapters with PVC-backed SQLite single-writer enforcement. Final completion remains blocked until an authorized operator can provide the required authenticated staging API/CLI evidence and independent MFA-backed disposable EKS E2E evidence.
next_steps: Complete and locally verify the typed AWS/EKS and Kubernetes lifecycle, package-level CLI tests, docs QA, and stale-doc cleanup without mutating a live target. Then have an authorized staging operator run documented authenticated API, Codex, and Claude Code smokes and an independent operator run the disposable EKS E2E; record only safe scalar evidence before enabling customer deploy.
human_actions: Can an authorized staging operator run the documented authenticated API, Codex, and Claude Code smokes using the protected staging caller token and provide only safe scalar outcomes?
Can the Identity Center administrator resolve #808 by enrolling an MFA method for the designated independent EKS validation operator?
